summary: Phase 149O.20L.7O.2D.2 -- HATP Principal/Signer Enrollment Contract Repair. FINAL DISPOSITION: CONTRACT REPAIRED, READY FOR SECOND INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION. Documentation-only contract architecture repair; zero Dell mutation, zero production .py bytes modified, zero enrollment, zero provisioning. Repaired HPSE-001 (docs/contracts/HATP_PRINCIPAL_SIGNER_ENROLLMENT_CONTRACT.md) from v1.0 to v1.1 in direct response to the two Blocking findings independently demonstrated by Phase 149O.20L.7O.2D.1. Re-read hatp_hardware_credentials.py, hatp_fido2_provider.py, hatp_piv_provider.py, hatp_providers.py, hatp_signing_ceremony.py, and human_approval_trusted_provenance.py fresh this session and reconfirmed both findings remained true at phase entry before editing any contract text. B-149O.20L.7O.2D.1-1 (HPSE-001 never named a required writer for hardware-credentials.json) is closed by naming a required future companion contract, HHCE-001 (HATP Hardware Credential Enrollment Contract, deliberately not authored this phase -- a scoped, minimum-coherent repair, not a full second contract), and, more importantly, by a new structural cross-registry precondition (HPSE-REQ-056, HPI-7): enroll_signer cannot write an active SignerRecord unless a matching active hardware-credential record already exists, checked live under a new fixed lock-acquisition ordering (HPSE-REQ-057) and a six-case partial-failure matrix (HPSE-REQ-058) covering every combination of credential-write/signer-write/audit/read-back/concurrency failure. B-149O.20L.7O.2D.1-2 (credential_identity()'s current-state characterization understated) is closed by revising HPSE-REQ-011 in place -- same requirement ID, never renumbered -- to disclose precisely that both Fido2HardwareProvider.credential_identity() and PivHardwareProvider.credential_identity() unconditionally raise HATPProviderUnavailableError regardless of device presence, plus two new requirements naming corrected target semantics (HPSE-REQ-059, semantic-output-only, no frozen implementation function name) and the additional hardware-provider-layer implementation prerequisite this fact requires, distinct from physical credential provisioning (HPSE-REQ-060). Also repaired, adjacent and low-risk per the two Non-Blocking findings judged worth immediate closure: documented the already-implemented producer/verifier hybrid trust model (verify_hatp_proof's live signer/principal/authority/binding cross-checks on every call) as settled architecture (HPSE-REQ-067/068), and the effective current revocation disposition that already fails closed at verification time without requiring DeploymentBinding rewrites (HPSE-REQ-069) -- neither changes any production code. Three further Non-Blocking findings were explicitly classified rather than silently dropped: one already resolved by the prior phase's own clarification (PrincipalRecord.revoked_at, unchanged), one explicitly deferred as a future implementation-hygiene concern (preview/create parity), and one explicitly deferred as HBDC-001's own pre-existing, unrelated staleness (with one additional newly-disclosed, deliberately-deferred stale cross-reference in HBDC-001's own header, left unrepaired per the explicit instruction not to bump HBDC-001 unless its own substantive text changes). 22 new requirements added strictly after HPSE-REQ-052 (HPSE-REQ-053 through HPSE-REQ-074); three existing requirements revised in place with an explicit inline revision marker, same requirement identity, never renumbered (HPSE-REQ-011, HPSE-REQ-045, HPSE-REQ-046); requirement count mechanically re-verified 001 through 074, sequential, no gaps, no duplicates. Two new security invariants added (HPI-7, HPI-8). A single composite implementation-readiness gate (HPSE-REQ-072) closes both findings jointly: enroll_signer cannot be considered implementation-ready until HHCE-001 exists and is independently verified, the selected hardware-provider implementation satisfies the corrected target semantics, a matching credential is actually registered, the target principal is active, and provider-profile consistency passes -- none of which hold today, so implementation correctly remains blocked by the contract's own text. HBDC-001 was not touched and remains v1.2 exactly as before. 35 new tests added in tests/test_phase_149o_20l_7o_2d_2_hatp_principal_signer_enrollment_contract_repair.py, all passing, mechanically re-verifying requirement numbering, revision-in-place discipline, the HHCE-001 disposition, the cross-registry invariant, the credential_identity() correction against live source (re-confirmed, not merely carried over from the prior phase's own claim), the signer_key_id equivalence, the composite gate, the closure mapping, the Non-Blocking disposition, and that no production source was modified. Recommended next: 149O.20L.7O.2D.3 -- HATP Principal/Signer Enrollment Contract Repair Independent Verification (must not implement anything). See docs/PHASE_149O_20L_7O_2D_2_HATP_PRINCIPAL_SIGNER_ENROLLMENT_CONTRACT_REPAIR.md for full detail.
